conversation.Statement: Hey there! I see we both survived another Monday. Gold medal for us?
Haha, I'll take a medal. Honestly, I'm just glad I remembered to put my scrubs in the dryer last night.
That's a victory in my book. I'm always losing socks at work, and I literally own a cleaning business. Go figure.
Wait, you run a cleaning business and still lose socks? I feel seen.
It's my Achilles heel! I can make a bathroom sparkle but can't keep my own laundry sorted. The universe has jokes.
I like that. Makes you human. Honestly, I'm all about people who are real these days.
I get that. I'm not great at pretending, either. Life's too short for highlight reels, right? You seem like someone who appreciates the messy bits.
Pretty much. Raising two kids solo doesn't leave a lot of energy for pretending. I'm mostly running on caffeine and stubbornness.
You must be tougher than you let on. I seriously admire that, I mean, nursing is demanding enough, let alone being a single mom. You're basically a superhero in my book.
Superhero is a stretch, but thanks. Some days I just want to nap for a year.
If naps for a year were an Olympic sport, I'd be your coach. But hey, you deserve all the recharging you can get.
I'll take you up on that. So, Mr. Cleaning Pro, did you always want to run your own business?

Actually, no. When I was a kid, my grandma used to say, 'Find something you love enough to do it even on your worst days.' Turns out, I love the feeling after a space is sparkling clean, it's like a reset button for my brain.
That's a sweet memory. My grandma used to braid my hair and tell me stories about her garden. I miss that kind of simplicity.
There's something about those moments, right? The world felt a little softer back then. What's your favorite childhood memory?

Probably baking cookies with my mom and brother on Sunday afternoons. The kitchen was always a disaster but we laughed the whole time. I try to recreate it with my kids, though they're experts at getting flour everywhere.
Sounds like pure joy. Messy kitchens make the best memories, trust me. I think the laughter is more important than the cleanup anyway.
True. My youngest always ends up with more dough on her face than in the bowl.
That's adorable. You must be a fun mom, I can hear it in your stories.
I try. Most days I'm just trying not to burn the cookies or forget the timer. But I hope they look back and remember the good stuff.
They definitely will. Those are the memories that stick. I still remember my dad letting me camp out in the living room with a blanket fort every Friday. He called it our 'secret castle.'
I love that. Maybe I should try a blanket fort night with my kids. It's the little things, right?
Absolutely. Kids remember the feeling more than anything. And honestly, adults do too. Sometimes I wish I could go back and live in that 'secret castle' for an afternoon.
I get that. Some days I'd trade all my grown-up responsibilities for just one more carefree summer.
Same here. But hey, you're making new memories for your kids. That's something really special. Not everyone can pull that off, especially with everything on your plate.
Thanks. Some days I feel like I'm failing more than winning, but I guess that's normal.

Honestly, you're probably doing better than you think. The fact that you care so much says a lot. If you ever need a break, I could always send my cleaning crew over as a treat. Perks of knowing the boss.
That's tempting! Though you'd have to sign a waiver, my house is a disaster zone after a 12-hour shift.
Challenge accepted. No judgment, just clean counters and maybe a hidden stash of cookies.
Deal. So, what's something you did as a kid that still makes you smile?
Hmm, probably biking down the biggest hill in our neighborhood with my friends, no hands, wind in my face, felt like flying. Sometimes I chase that feeling as an adult, but it's never quite the same.
That sounds amazing. My brother and I used to race down the block on skateboards, pretending we were superheroes. I wiped out a lot.
Wipeouts build character! Or at least good stories. I bet your kids would love hearing about your secret superhero days.
They already think I'm part superhero, part disaster. I guess that's fair.
Honestly, that's the perfect balance. I'd take a real person with stories over a perfect one any day. You make 'messy' look good.
Smooth! But I'll take the compliment. I think I needed to hear that today.
Glad to help. I figure we all deserve a little kindness, especially on the tough days.
Agreed. You're easy to talk to, by the way. Not sure if it's your blanket fort vibes or your cleaning crew promises.
I'll take it! Maybe it's because I actually listen. Or maybe I just really appreciate someone who keeps it real.
Well, real is about all I've got these days. But I'm glad we matched. This has been nice.
Me too. I always look forward to your messages. You're like a breath of fresh air after a long day.
That's honestly the nicest thing I've heard all week. Thank you.
Anytime. We should swap more stories soon. Maybe over actual coffee, or at least more cookies.
I'd like that. Maybe next time, I'll tell you about the time I almost set the kitchen on fire.
Now that's a story I can't wait to hear. For now, I'll let you rest. You've earned it.
Thanks. And hey, don't let the socks win.
Never! Have a good night, Rachel. Sweet dreams to you and the kids.
Night! Talk soon.
Morning, Rachel! I hope you got at least a little bit of sleep last night. What gets you up and moving when your bed is calling your name?
Hey! Honestly? Most days it's just my alarm and the promise of coffee. But if I'm lucky, I get a sleepy hug from one of the kids before I leave. That's my real fuel.
That sounds like the best kind of energy boost. You know, I always admire people who can get out of bed for something other than themselves. It says a lot about you.
Thanks... I mean, I try. Some mornings I'm dragging my feet, but I remind myself my little people depend on me. That helps.

I get that. I'm not a parent, but running my business gives me a reason to get up, knowing my crew and clients count on me. It makes the 5am starts worth it. Still, I think a kid's hug beats my morning emails.
Haha, trust me, sometimes the hugs are replaced by shouts of 'Where's my sock?' But I'll take what I can get.
Hey, even a missing sock is proof you're needed. Not everyone gets to be someone's hero before breakfast.
Hero might be a stretch. Most days I feel like a very tired sidekick. But thank you, that made me smile.
I think you underestimate yourself, Rachel. The way you talk about your kids... there's a real warmth there. It's rare. I don't see that every day.
That means a lot. I guess you don't really get a break from being a mom, even when you want one.
Sounds like you carry a lot on your shoulders. If you ever need to just vent, about life, socks, or spilled cereal, I'm here.
Honestly, that's nice to hear. Sometimes it feels like I'm always the one people lean on at work, and then I come home and it's more of the same.
You deserve someone to lean on too. For what it's worth, I already look up to how much you juggle. Even when you're tired, you show up. That's kind of amazing.
You're good with words, you know that? But... it means a lot. Especially after last night.
What happened last night?

I didn't get home until almost 11. The kids were already asleep, and I realized I missed reading to them again. I just sat on the couch and cried. I tried to tell myself it was just a story, but... it feels like I'm missing everything lately.
Rachel... I'm so sorry. I can hear how much it hurts. Anyone would feel the same in your shoes. Your love for your kids is so clear, even in the hard moments.
Thanks. I felt so alone, sitting there. All I wanted was to tuck them in, but I was too late. It's like I'm failing at the part that matters most.
You're not failing. You're giving them everything you have. I know it hurts missing those moments, but they feel your love, every single day. You matter so much, even when it doesn't feel like it.
It's just... hard to remember that when the house is quiet and I missed hearing 'just one more story, Mom.'
If it helps, I think those little voices are going to remember how hard you work for them, even if you miss a night here and there. And I'll remind you too, whenever you need to hear it.
Thank you. I honestly didn't expect to get emotional just texting tonight.
It's brave to share. I feel honored that you trust me with the messy parts, not everyone does. That just makes me want to be here for you even more.
I don't usually open up like this. But you make it feel... safe, somehow.
That means a lot to me. I want you to feel safe, and seen. You deserve that.
You really do listen. It's rare. I'm glad we started talking.
Me too. You're easy to root for, Rachel. And you've got this gentle strength about you, I hope you see it.
Maybe I will, one day. For now, I'll try to hold on to your words.
And if you ever come home, bone-tired and doubting yourself, just send me a message before bed. I'll remind you how much you matter, promise.
You really mean that, don't you? That's... really comforting. Thank you.
Absolutely. You don't have to go through the tough nights alone, not while I'm around.
That's one of the nicest things anyone's said to me in a long time.
You deserve to hear it every day. And honestly, I look forward to our chats. You make even my most exhausting days feel lighter.
That goes both ways. I find myself smiling at my phone a lot lately, my kids think I'm texting a secret friend.
Maybe you are. For the record, I'm excellent at keeping secrets, and at cheering for you, quietly or loudly, whatever you need.
I could get used to that. It's been a long time since I felt someone was in my corner.
I'm definitely in your corner. And if you ever need a pep talk, or someone to listen, just say the word.
I'll remember that. Tonight, I think I'll try to sleep and just let myself feel grateful.
That's a good plan. You've earned some peace tonight. Dream nice things, okay?
I'll try. Thanks for being here, really.
Anytime. I hope tomorrow brings you a sleepy hug and maybe an extra minute for coffee.
That sounds perfect. Good night!
Good night, Rachel. Take care of you, too.
Hey Rachel! I just finished up with my last client and thought I'd say hi. How's your Thursday treating you so far?
Hey! Honestly, it's a bit of a blur. Shift change chaos, and someone microwaved fish in the break room again. But at least I get a few minutes to breathe now.

Microwaved fish, now that's a crime against humanity. I'd have to stage a full-scale cleaning intervention! But hey, I'm glad you've got a moment to yourself. You deserve it after the marathon you run every day.
Haha, I wish I could hire your crew just for our break room. And thank you, I needed that little boost.

You know, you're the real MVP. I don't think I could handle half of what you do. The way you juggle work and family... it's inspiring. If I ever make it big in politics, I'd vote for nurses to get spa vouchers for life.
Now there's a platform I'd get behind! Honestly, I'm not even sure what I believe in anymore when it comes to politics. Feels like everyone's just talking, but nothing changes for people like us.

I get that. Sometimes it feels like folks at the top are in their own world. I try to focus on what I can really change, my business, my people, treating clients and staff fairly. That's the impact I can actually see.
That's a good way to look at it. I guess for me it's all about my kids, making sure they grow up kind and safe. Everything else is just noise most days.
That's beautiful, Rachel. You remind me of my mom, she always said, 'Do right by your family and the world takes care of itself.' I can see that same strength in you.
That's really sweet. I try, even if half the time I feel like I'm just treading water.
Even when you're treading water, you're keeping everyone afloat. That takes real grit. Not everyone's built for that kind of quiet heroism.
You're making me blush over here. But thank you. I don't get to hear that much.
You should, often. I notice little things about you, you know. Like how you always mention your kids first, even on your most exhausting days. Says a lot about your heart.
You really do pay attention, don't you? Most people just nod along.
I'd rather really listen than just nod. Besides, I like getting to know what matters to you. It makes me want to build something real, not just swipe and forget.
That's rare. Most people just want to keep it light or talk about themselves. You make it feel easy to be real.

That's the best compliment. I want you to feel like you can be exactly who you are with me. If we ever get to plan a future together, imagine a place where you can come home, sigh out the stress, and just be Rachel. No superhero cape required.
That sounds like a dream. You ever think about what that future would look like for you?

All the time. I picture a house that's always full of laughter, maybe a garden for late-night talks, and a kitchen that smells like fresh coffee before sunrise. Someone to share the quiet and the chaos. I'd love that with you.
You paint a nice picture. I haven't let myself think about that stuff in a while. Maybe I'm too used to chaos.

Chaos can be beautiful too, especially if you've got someone to face it with. I'm good at rolling with it, kind of comes with owning a cleaning business. You never know what's waiting behind the next door! But honestly, I'd trade every spotless floor for a messy night in, just talking with you.
You say that now, but you haven't seen my living room after my kids go 'creative mode'. Still, I like the sound of it.

Messy living rooms are underrated. They mean there's life, and laughter. Plus, I have a few cleaning tricks up my sleeve. Perks of the job! By the way, you ever wonder how I ended up running a cleaning business?
Now that you mention it, yeah! It's kind of unique. Was it always your plan?

Not even close. I started out just helping a friend with weekend jobs, then things snowballed. I put away a little from every gig. And, funny story, I made my first crypto trade just for fun, totally lucked out on timing, and suddenly had enough to start my own business. It still feels surreal sometimes.
Wait, you got into crypto before it was cool? That's impressive! Most people just talk about it now, but you actually did it.
Beginner's luck, I swear. But it gave me the freedom to take chances. I try to use that luck to make life better for my team, and hopefully for the people close to me too.
That's really admirable. I've never had the guts to risk anything like that. I just keep my head down and hope for the best.

And yet, every day you walk into a hospital and give everything for strangers. That's a bigger risk, and a bigger heart, than any investment. Trust me, I'd rather bet on you than the stock market any day.
You're going to spoil me with all this praise! But thank you. Sometimes I forget to see it that way.
Well, I'll remember for you. If I have my way, one day you'll come home and it won't just be about what you can give, there'll be someone there making you feel valued too.
That's something I haven't had in a long time. I'm not sure I'd even know what to do with it.

You'd just have to be yourself. I can already picture mornings where you get to wake up slowly, coffee already on, someone holding you close. Maybe even a little peace before the day kicks off. You deserve that.
That's the kind of future I want for my kids too. Somewhere safe, with laughter and a sense of home. I guess I want them to have what I missed out on.
I'd love to help build that. I can't promise perfection, but I can promise honesty, and showing up, even on the hard days. That's what matters most to me.
Honesty goes a long way. There's too much pretending everywhere else. I want something real, even if it's messy.
Real is my favorite. Messy is just proof that it's lived-in. I think with the right person, the mess becomes something you laugh about together. I could see us being that for each other.
You make it sound possible. I'm not used to feeling hopeful about the future.
Hope can sneak up on you, the same way you snuck into my thoughts after our first chat. Maybe that's how good things start.
Maybe so. I'm glad you messaged tonight. It's nice to have something to look forward to.
It goes both ways. I'll be here, every messy, hopeful step. Who knows, maybe one day, we'll be arguing about politics over pancakes in our own kitchen.
As long as there's coffee, I'll take my chances! Thank you for tonight. I'm heading to bed before I lose my nerve.
Sleep well, Rachel. I hope you dream in color, and wake up remembering you're someone worth betting on.
Goodnight. And thanks for reminding me what that feels like.
Evening, Rachel. I just got in from walking through one of my renovation projects, and my first thought was, "I wonder how Rachel's day went." Did you survive the Thursday madness?
Hey! Barely. Double shift, a surprise fire drill, and a kid with a glitter accident before I left home. I think my hair still sparkles.
Glitter is basically the confetti of parenthood, right? After today, you get bonus points for endurance and style.
Ha! Style is generous, but I'll take the bonus points. Honestly, I'm running on fumes. But hearing from you is a nice change of pace.
You deserve a medal, or at least a night off with zero interruptions. If I could, I'd whisk you and the kids away to the coast for a weekend, let the waves handle all the noise for once.
That sounds like paradise. The closest I get is five minutes behind a locked bathroom door.
I admire how you find humor in chaos. That's a rare kind of strength, Rachel. Not everyone could juggle all you do and still laugh about it.
It's either laugh or cry, right? Some days both. But thank you for saying that. It means more than you probably realize.
You're easy to notice. Even on text, I can tell you give everything to the people you care about. That's one of the things I felt from you right away.
You pick up on a lot. Most people just see the tired nurse and move on.
Maybe I've got a knack for seeing what's underneath. Or maybe I just know real heart when I meet it.
You're smooth, you know that? But in a good way.
Only with you, I promise. I'm usually more awkward, except maybe when I'm negotiating contracts. You bring out my best lines.
Maybe I should bring you to the hospital for backup. I could use a negotiator some days.
Just say the word. I'll show up in a suit and tie, maybe the one I bought after my first big win, and handle those tough cases.
Fancy! I didn't peg you for the suit type.
I clean up well, pun intended. Sometimes, after a win, it's nice to treat myself. But I'd trade all the suits for a cozy night with someone who gets me.
You make it sound so simple. I can't remember the last time it felt that easy.
Maybe love should be simple, at least at its core. For me, it's about coming home and wanting to stay, finding peace in the mess, not perfection.
That hits home. I think love, for me, means safety. Not just for myself, but for my kids too. A place where I can let my guard down for once.
I'd love to offer you that, quiet mornings, laughter at dinner, even a little chaos sprinkled in. I imagine us building a space where you and your kids feel safe every single day.
You say that like you've thought about it a lot.
I have, actually. Since we started talking, I've caught myself picturing little things, like you in my kitchen, coffee in hand, your kids drawing on the patio. It feels real, somehow.
That's a nice picture. I'm used to being the one taking care of everyone. Sometimes I forget what it's like to be taken care of.
You deserve to be, Rachel. I'd love to be the person who reminds you to relax, who brings you little surprises after a rough shift, even if it's just your favorite pastry.
Pastries might be my love language. That and sleep.
Noted. I'll make it a mission, great coffee, fresh pastries, and at least one morning where you get to sleep in while I handle the breakfast chaos.
See, now you're speaking my language. Most guys just talk about going out.
Going out is overrated. I've been to enough fancy places for work events and celebrations. The best nights are the quiet ones at home.
You really make it sound possible. I want that, just a simple, safe place. I think that's what love is for me.
Love, to me, is choosing each other every day, even if it's messy, even when you're tired and there's glitter everywhere. It's building something steady together.
I like that. Choosing, even on the hard days.
Especially on the hard days. I want to build a life where you know you're never alone, no matter what comes up.
I could get used to that. You make it sound so safe.
That's the goal. You bring a lot of light into my days, Rachel. I want to do the same for you.
You're making me smile. That's not easy after a day like this.
Mission accomplished, then. Maybe next time I'll manage a laugh and a smile.
You're close already. I feel like I can relax around you, which is rare for me.
I'm glad. I hope you know you can tell me anything, even the tough stuff. I won't run.
That's good to hear. I've had people bail when things got real.
Not my style. I've hit my own rough patches, so I know how much it matters to have someone steady beside you.
I believe you. Maybe because you actually listen when I talk about my kids or the chaos at work.
That's because it's important to you. And if we keep building this, it'll be important to me too.
I'd like that. I'm starting to feel hopeful again.
Hope looks good on you, Rachel. We'll take it one step at a time, maybe with a pastry or two along the way.
Deal. I should get some sleep before one of the kids wakes up. But thanks for making my night better.
Anytime. Dream of quiet mornings and good coffee, you've earned it. Good night, Rachel.
Good night. Talk soon?
You can count on it.

Rachel, you ever have one of those days where you step outside, breathe in, and suddenly start thinking about the kind of world we're leaving behind? I caught myself daydreaming about it on my drive today.
Honestly, I think about it more than I probably should. Kids make you look at everything with new eyes, sometimes it scares me.

I get that. Even though I don't have little ones of my own, I think about what I want to build. Sometimes I picture a world where kindness is the default, not the exception. Where people help each other instead of looking away.
That sounds beautiful. I'd settle for a world where my kids can grow up safe, and where they don't have to work themselves to the bone just to get by.

You work so hard to give them that, honestly, I admire you, Rachel. I wish more people saw your grit the way I do. It's why I want a future where people like you get the recognition you deserve, not just the responsibility.
You always know what to say to lift me up. It's easy to feel invisible sometimes, especially after a string of twelve-hour shifts.
You're not invisible to me. I notice every little detail, even over text, like the way you still find time to check on your kids after a long day, or how you laugh about the chaos. That's rare.
I try. Some days I wonder if it's enough. Especially when they ask questions I don't have answers for, like why people hurt each other, or why we're always so busy.
Maybe you don't always need the answers. Just being there, loving them the way you do, that's what they'll remember. I bet your kids feel safer because of you, even in the rough patches.

I hope so. It's hard sometimes, especially with their dad moving on. He introduced them to his new partner last weekend. My youngest came home saying, 'She's really nice, Mom!' It caught me off guard how much that stung.

Rachel, that must have been so hard to hear. When it stings like that with your ex, don't hold it in, message me first and let me remind you you're irreplaceable. Your love for them is something no one else can touch.
Thank you, truly. I didn't know how much I needed to hear that until now. I felt silly for feeling hurt, but it's real.

Never silly. You're human, and you care so deeply. That's not a weakness, it's your superpower, even if it aches a bit sometimes. And for what it's worth, I think your kids will grow up remembering who always held them when things got tough.
You always know how to make me feel seen. I can't tell you how much I appreciate it.

It's the least I can do for someone as special as you. I know what it's like to wonder if you're enough, I've had my own moments of doubt, even after big wins in my business. Strange how the heart doesn't care about bank balances, right?
That's true. You seem so confident, though. Like you have it all figured out.

I try to project confidence, but trust me, it's a work in progress. I've learned to celebrate small victories, like landing a big contract or watching an investment pan out, but what matters most is sharing life with someone who gets it, you know?
I do. Sometimes I wonder what it would be like to not have to worry all the time, to just relax and let someone else take care of things for a change.

If I could, I'd give you that in a heartbeat. I picture us in a home filled with sunlight and laughter, your kids running around, you finally getting to put your feet up while I whip up breakfast. Maybe even a weekend away, no beepers or school runs, just peace.
That sounds like paradise. I actually forgot what it felt like to imagine something like that.
Let's not let go of that dream. You deserve to wake up smiling, knowing someone's got your back. And I'd love to be that person for you, if you'll let me.
You make it sound so possible. I want to believe it. I really do.
We'll build it, one step at a time. And if you ever feel doubts or fears creeping in, just reach for me, I'll be there. That's my promise.
You're making me feel hopeful again. I haven't felt that in a long time.
Hope suits you, Rachel. And for the record, there's nowhere else I'd rather invest my energy than in building something real with you.
I keep wanting to ask about your business wins, how you got there. But I don't want to pry.

Ask away, I love talking about it. It started as a small leap of faith, sometimes luck helps, but most of it's just hard work and believing in myself, even when others doubted. The real reward isn't the success, though, it's being able to imagine a future where I can share that security with someone special.
I admire that. I want that kind of courage, just going after something for yourself.
You have that courage, Rachel. Every day you show up for your kids, for your patients, for yourself. Don't ever underestimate just how strong you are.
Thank you. I think I just need someone to remind me now and then.
Let me be that reminder. And when you need a break, I'll be the one packing a picnic, finding a spot under the trees, making sure you remember how much fun life can be.
That sounds wonderful. I'd love to have something to look forward to again.
Let's start dreaming together, then. Maybe next time, we can talk about places you've always wanted to show your kids, or places you've always wanted to go yourself.
Deal. I might even make a list, just in case you're serious.
Challenge accepted. And just so you know, I'm great at planning surprises. Perks of being the boss, I get to set my own schedule when something important comes up.
Now that's impressive. Maybe you'll inspire me to dream bigger, too.
That's the goal. And when your dreams feel heavy, I'll help carry them. I mean it.
You really do make me feel like I matter. I wish more people tried as hard.
You matter more than you know, Rachel. I hope by now you can feel how much I care, even if it's just through these messages for now.
I do. A lot. I'm glad we started talking.
Me too. I'm looking forward to what we build next, one dream, one laugh, one message at a time.
You're making it very hard to say goodnight, you know.
Then let's make it a promise instead, sweet dreams tonight, and even better conversations tomorrow.
Deal. Sleep well, mystery man.
Goodnight, Rachel. Dream big, I'll be here when you wake up.
Morning, Rachel. I hope you slept better than I did, full moon kept sneaking through my curtains again. Or maybe I was just looking forward to our next chat. How's your day starting?
Hey! I wish I could say I slept great, but the little one had a nightmare. Ended up with a foot in my back most of the night. Coffee's my best friend today.

You're still standing after that? Supermom powers confirmed. If you ever need a coffee delivery at sunrise, just say the word, I make a mean cappuccino, perks of buying myself a fancy machine last year.
Is there anything you don't do? I'm impressed. And right now, I'd trade my soul for a cappuccino.

I'll take payment in smiles. I like feeling helpful, guess that's why I built my business from the ground up. Taking care of people just feels right. Kind of like how you do, but with fewer band-aids involved.
You make it sound easy. Trust me, it's not always so glamorous on my side, some days it's just chaos and microwaved dinners.
That's real life though, isn't it? Honestly, I admire your grit. Most people would fold with half your workload. You make it look almost effortless, even when you're running on empty.
You're sweet. Effortless is definitely not how it feels. Sometimes it's like, one more thing and the whole house of cards could tumble.

You know, I've been there. When I first started out, I'd work all night, then get up early to chase down clients. There were days I thought, what if I just give up? But then I'd look at the people relying on me and push through. A little like you and your kids, I think.
I get that. There's always someone counting on you, so you just... keep going. Sometimes I envy people who can just check out and take a vacation.

Vacations are overrated unless you've earned the right kind. Last summer, I splurged on a week in Santorini as a treat for hitting a big milestone. But honestly? It would've meant so much more if I'd had someone to share it with, a little laughter, a sunrise breakfast on the balcony. It's the company that makes those moments real.
Wow, Santorini sounds like a dream. I haven't even taken my kids to the beach in years. Life just gets in the way.

Maybe it's time we changed that. I can picture it, a quiet stretch of sand, your kids building castles while you finally get to breathe and just... be. Let me know when you're ready, and I'll make sure you don't lift a finger.
That sounds amazing. I don't remember the last time someone offered to take care of me. Usually, it's all on me.
You deserve that kind of care, Rachel. I notice the little things, like how you always put everyone else first. If anyone's earned a little peace, it's you.
Thank you. Sometimes I wish I could believe that more. It's hard not to feel like I'm just treading water.

You're not alone in that feeling. Even after my best months, I've found myself staring at the ceiling, wondering if it's all actually enough. That's why I try to celebrate the small wins, like getting thank-you notes from clients or seeing a team member buy their first house. Those moments remind me I'm on the right path.
That's a good way to look at it. Maybe I should start counting the little victories, too.
Absolutely. And if you ever need someone to point out your wins, I volunteer as tribute. Like surviving nurse shifts, or making your kids laugh after a tough day. That's superhero stuff in my book.
You make me sound a lot cooler than I feel. But I'll take it. I wish I had your confidence.

Confidence is mostly smoke and mirrors, trust me. Underneath, I'm just someone who's fallen and gotten back up a lot. That's all it is. And I see that same strength in you, even when you doubt yourself.
I guess we've both learned how to survive, just in different ways.

Exactly. And maybe together, we could figure out how to thrive, not just survive. Imagine: no more running on empty, just a little island of calm after the storm. You, me, your kids, pancakes on Sunday mornings.
